subtitle: One-Shot Sample Player
tagline: Loads a WAV, AIFF, FLAC, or Ogg sample and fires it from the panel or from an automatable trigger, with click-free retriggering and a soft stop.

body.lead: TB AudioPlayer is a one-shot sample player. Load a sample, then fire it with the PLAY button or with the host's Trigger parameter. Each shot starts the sample from the beginning; a new shot starts at once while the previous one fades out over 50 ms, so retriggering stays click-free.

body.p: It converts the sample to the session's sample rate, plays it back in mono or stereo, and recalls the selected sample with your session. There are no volume, pitch, loop, or speed controls: it does one job, precisely.

ul: One-shot playback of WAV, AIFF, FLAC, and Ogg files
Automatable Trigger parameter that fires on a rising edge from 0 to 1
Click-free 50 ms fades on retrigger and STOP
Sample-rate conversion for correct pitch at any session rate
Display of the file name, sample rate, channels, and length
Session recall, presets, and undo and redo of the sample selection
VST3 instrument and standalone application for Windows

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB AudioPlayer 1.0.0 for Windows (VST3 and standalone). There is no macOS build at the time of writing.

ol: Insert TB AudioPlayer on an instrument track, or start the standalone application.
Click `BROWSE` {{6}} and choose a WAV, AIFF, FLAC, or Ogg file. The display {{3}} shows its name, sample rate, channels, and length, and the status {{7}} reads Ready.
Click `PLAY` {{4}} to hear the sample from the beginning, and `STOP` {{5}} to fade all playback out over 50 ms.
To fire the sample from your DAW, automate the Trigger parameter: each change from 0 to 1 starts it. Return Trigger to 0 before the next shot.

Chooses the sample. MP3 is not supported, and a decoded sample can use up to 256 MiB of memory.
Fires on a rising edge from 0 to 1. Return it to 0 before the next shot. Trigger is saved as 0 with the state.

note.text: The sample is referenced by its file path; it is not embedded in the session or in presets. If you move or rename the file, select it again with BROWSE.

body.p: The preset list holds Init and your user presets. Save stores the current state, including the sample path, as a .tbap file. Undo and Redo step through sample selections.

recipes.title: Spot effects on cue
recipes.use: Hits, risers, or voice clips at exact song positions.
settings: 0 → 1 at each cue, back to 0 after
steps: Draw short automation pulses so Trigger returns to 0 before the next cue.

recipes.title: Live playback
recipes.use: Firing jingles or clips by hand, for example in a stream.
steps: STOP ends the clip with a 50 ms fade instead of a hard cut.

recipes.title: Layered hit
recipes.use: A sub drop or impact layered with a drum hit.
steps: Balance the layer with the track fader; TB AudioPlayer has no volume control.

body.p: PLAY, STOP, BROWSE, and the preset functions are panel controls, not host parameters. The sample path is stored in the plug-in state.

rows: First release: a compact one-shot sample player for WAV, AIFF, FLAC, and Ogg files with browser loading and immediate playback; an automatable rising-edge Trigger; click-free 50 ms retrigger and Stop fades; sample-rate conversion; state recall; presets; Undo and Redo.
